blocks.content: Article 32 is the very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it.

rows: Protects personal liberty against arbitrary detention
Directs performance of a mandatory legal duty
Preventive; stops lower court from exceeding jurisdiction
Preventive & curative; quashes illegal lower court orders
Persons occupying public offices of substance
Prevents illegal usurpation of a public office

items: Mandamus cannot be issued against private individuals, the President of India, or State Governors.
Prohibition is purely preventive, whereas Certiorari is both preventive and curative in nature.
Supreme Court writ jurisdiction under Article 32 is a Fundamental Right itself, whereas High Court writ jurisdiction under Article 226 is discretionary.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 32 guarantees the right to move the Supreme Court for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
The Supreme Court can issue five types of writs: Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, and Quo-Warranto.
Habeas Corpus is the only writ that can be issued against both public authorities and private individuals.
High Courts under Article 226 have a wider writ jurisdiction than the Supreme Court under Article 32, as High Courts can issue writs for ordinary legal rights as well.
Quo-Warranto can be sought by any interested person, even if they are not the aggrieved party.
